newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Chevron begins sending Tengiz oil through Caucasus.
newsitem.headline: Chevron begins sending Tengiz oil through Caucasus.

text.p: U.S. Chevron Corp has begun exporting some oil from its big TengizChevroil (TCO) project in Kazakhstan by rail through Azerbaijan and Georgia, a senior company official said on Thursday.

Richard Matzke, president of Chevron Overseas Petroleum Inc, said a maiden shipment of 20,000 tonnes of crude had left the Azeri capital Baku for the Georgian Black Sea port of Batumi and on to western markets.

He said that if the delivery was successful, Chevron would use the route to ship 100,000 tonnes of oil per month (about 24,000 barrels per day). "We are loading rail trains today in Baku," he told a news conference.
"We would hope that if the system is capable and if all of the partners are willing, we could move it at 100,000 tonnes a month later this year."
The oil is brought to Baku from Kazakhstan's Tengiz field by tanker across the Caspian Sea, and then loaded onto rail cars and sent to Batumi.

Most Tengiz production is exported via Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk, but the pipeline has only enough capacity to handle about half of Chevron's output at Tengiz of six million tonnes per year, Matzke said.
The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) plans to build a $1.2-$1.5 billion link from Tengiz to Novorossiisk to increase export capacity, but the line will not be ready for at least several years.
The lack of pipeline capacity has thwarted Chevron's output plans at Tengiz and led it to seek additional export options.
"We are active partners in the CPC," Matzke said. "This is a new pipeline system which doesn't currently exist. In the most optimistic scenario, it will take two and a half to three years to finish.
"We are trying to find a reasonable solution to move Caspian oil to world markets."
Chevron has also turned to shipping oil by rail to Novorossiisk and to Odessa in Ukraine.

Matzke has said earlier that Chevron was also interested in transporting oil from Tengiz by tanker to Baku and then through an existing pipeline to Georgia's Black Sea coast, but this route is not operational and needs extensive refurbishing.
Production at Tengiz by Chevron and its equity partner Mobil Corp is expected to reach 700,000 barrels per day by 2010.
